title: Deep hyper-pipelining for high frequency target
decision: Design a much deeper pipeline (approximately 2× the P6 microarchitecture, ~20-stage misprediction pipeline) with fewer gates of logic per stage to enable a >1.6× higher frequency target on the same process technology.
alternatives_or_rejected: Shallower pipeline like the P6 family that keeps higher instructions-per-clock efficiency at a given frequency.
rationale: Higher clock rates more than compensate for the lower per-clock efficiency caused by longer misprediction and cache-miss penalties; the frequency headroom was the primary performance lever for the NetBurst family.
outcome: Industry-leading clock rates (1.5 GHz at introduction) and the highest SPECint_base scores of any processor at the time, despite deeper recovery penalties.

title: Execution Trace Cache as primary L1 instruction cache
decision: Replace a conventional instruction cache with an Execution Trace Cache that stores already-decoded uops in program-order traces (up to 12K uops) and delivers up to three uops per clock.
alternatives_or_rejected: A traditional IA-32 instruction cache that requires repeated decoding of variable-length instructions on every fetch.
rationale: IA-32 instructions are cumbersome to decode (variable length, many options); caching decoded uops bypasses the decoder most of the time, reduces misprediction latency, and allows the decoder itself to be simplified to one instruction per cycle.
outcome: Trace Cache hit rate comparable to an 8–16 KB conventional I-cache; decoder is off the critical path for most execution, supporting the deep pipeline.

title: Reduced second FP/SSE execution port
decision: Provide only one full FP/SSE execution unit plus a simple second port limited to FP/SSE moves and store-data primitives, rather than two full-featured units.
alternatives_or_rejected: Two complete FP/SSE execution units (the early design point).
rationale: Two full units cost substantial die area and power while delivering only modest extra performance for most FP/SSE applications; the simple second port captured most of the benefit of a second full port at far lower cost. Many FP workloads interleave multiplies and adds and can keep a single complex unit busy.
outcome: Most of the performance of a dual full-port design at significantly lower area and power; the cost/performance tradeoff was judged favorable.

title: Double-clocked (2×) ALUs for rapid integer execution
decision: Clock the basic integer ALUs at twice the core frequency so that simple integer operations can complete in half a processor clock cycle.
alternatives_or_rejected: Single-speed ALUs running at the main core clock (as in prior designs).
rationale: Basic integer operations are critical to overall IPC; running them at 2× frequency effectively provides higher throughput and lower latency for the most common operations without requiring a still-deeper main pipeline.
outcome: Rapid Execution Engine capable of high integer throughput supporting the overall NetBurst performance targets.

title: Low-latency L1 data cache design
decision: Implement a new low-latency L1 data-cache organization and algorithms optimized for the deep pipeline and high frequency.
alternatives_or_rejected: Conventional higher-latency L1 data-cache designs sized or timed as in the P6 family.
rationale: With a deeper pipeline, load-to-use latency becomes a larger fraction of the critical path; minimizing L1 data-cache latency was essential to keep dependent integer operations from stalling.
outcome: Lower effective load latency that helped preserve IPC despite the longer overall pipeline.
